name: Cognizant (GenC, GenC Pro, GenC Next)
tagline: GenC programme tracks from GenC to GenC Next

overview.about: Cognizant hires freshers through its Generation Cognizant (GenC) programme. Tracks reported include GenC (programmer analyst trainee), GenC Pro and GenC Next (higher packages, harder coding/skill tests), plus GenC Elevate for some campuses. Assessments combine communication, aptitude and skill-based technical tests, followed by interviews. Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.
eligibility: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech/MCA/M.Sc for engineering tracks; some windows open to 3-year degrees (BCA/B.Sc etc.) — check each notice
Typically 60% or more (or 6.0 CGPA) in 10th, 12th/diploma and graduation (as reported)

pattern.paper: Aptitude — quant, logical; game-based modules reported

overview.frequency: Campus drives in season plus off-campus windows announced on the careers site

cards.title: Tracks
points: GenC: entry track; aptitude + communication focus
GenC Pro: higher band; adds a skill-based technical test
GenC Next: highest band; coding-heavy, harder problems
Track names and packages can change by season — Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Flow
cards.body: Typical sequence: communication assessment → aptitude (incl. game-based modules) → skill-based technical test for Pro/Next → technical + HR interview.

cards.title: Communication assessment
cards.body: Read-aloud, listen-and-repeat, sentence building and short comprehension, scored by software. Clear, unhurried speech wins.

cards.title: Aptitude
cards.body: Quant (percentages, ratios, time-work, P&C), logical (series, puzzles, arrangements) and game-based tasks testing memory, attention and pattern recognition.

cards.title: No service bond
cards.body: Cognizant states GenC has no service bonds. Read the offer letter for training and location terms anyway.

cards.title: Quant sample
cards.body:
Q: Two numbers are in the ratio 3:5 and their sum is 64. Find the larger.
Total parts 8 → one part 8 → larger = 5 × 8 = 40.

cards.q: Which GenC track typically has the hardest coding assessment?
cards.explain: GenC Next is the highest band and the most coding-heavy.

cards.title: What is tested
points: SQL: write queries on a given schema
Code debugging: fix small buggy snippets

cards.title: SQL style
cards.body:
Employees(id, name, dept, salary). Highest salary per department:
SELECT dept, MAX(salary)
FROM Employees
GROUP BY dept;

cards.title: Debugging style
Coding topics
cards.body: Arrays, strings, hashing, sorting, two pointers; for GenC Next also DP, graphs and greedy problems at medium difficulty.

cards.title: Debugging speed
cards.body: Look first at loop bounds, wrong operators (= vs ==), integer division, missing return statements and off-by-one indices — they cover most debugging items.

cards.title: Partial credit
cards.body: Each coding problem is usually scored by test cases. Submit a working brute force early, then optimise.

cards.q: Which SQL clause groups rows so that MAX(salary) is computed per department?
cards.explain: GROUP BY creates one group per department.

cards.title: Technical round
cards.body: Project walkthrough, OOP pillars with examples, SQL joins and a query, basic OS/CN, a small program. For GenC Next, expect DSA follow-ups on your coding solution.

cards.title: HR round
cards.body: Introduction, why Cognizant, relocation and shift flexibility, strengths/weaknesses, and document verification questions.

cards.title: Common question
cards.body: "Explain the difference between an abstract class and an interface with an example." → Shape (abstract class with shared colour field) vs Drawable (interface any class can implement).

cards.title: Know your resume
cards.body: Every technology listed is fair game. Prune skills you can't answer two questions on.

cards.title: Ask about training
cards.body: A good closing question: 'Which technology stream do GenC trainees typically get trained in?' It shows interest without sounding salary-focused.

cards.title: SQL in interviews
cards.body:
"Find employees who earn more than their manager."
SELECT e.name FROM Emp e JOIN Emp m ON e.manager_id = m.id WHERE e.salary > m.salary;  (a self join)

cards.q: 'Employees earning more than their manager' from one Emp table needs a:
cards.explain: The table is joined to itself on manager_id = id.

cards.q: Which closing question best suits an HR round?
options: "How soon can I get a hike?"
"What does the training plan look like for new GenC hires?"
cards.explain: It shows genuine interest in the role.
